record.question: Which clinical finding in a male trauma patient would be an indication for an RGU before attempting to insert a Foley catheter?
options: Blood at the urethral meatus (tip of the penis)
Inability to void after drinking fluids
record.explanation: Answer C: Blood at the urethral meatus (tip of the penis). Blood at the urethral meatus after trauma is a sign of possible urethral injury; retrograde urethrography should precede blind catheterization. Reference: https://www.radiologyinfo.org/en/info/voidcysto; https://www.radiologyinfo.org/en/info/safety-xray. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
